articles.title: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
articles.summary: Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at…

blocks.text: EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at sealing a breakthrough deal tackling Beijing’s record £1bn-a-day trade surplus by curbing its exports of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe.
Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team fly out on Wednesday and will be negotiating up to the wire in talks scheduled to start the following day and continue late into Friday.
Sources say they hope to achieve “tangible, meaningful and measurable” results before the meeting of EU leaders in Brussels on Thursday next week, where China is high on the agenda.

The main focus is on what has been described as a “proof of concept” pilot agreement involving one sector, which is expected to be cars, which could be scaled up for other sectors in the coming months.

Diplomatic efforts to avert a full-scale trade war started at the end of June, albeit with little hope that China could curb exports to the EU given its historic ability to pivot quickly any time trade barriers are put in its path. For example, after the EU imposed tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in October 2024 there was a boom in exports of hybrid cars, which were not subject to tariffs.
Last month, the EU asked China to voluntarily restrict hybrid exports to address soaring sales, warning that if they did not restrict them, safeguards – which could include quotas – could be enacted.

It is not known what China’s response was. But sources say the mood in talks has changed as EU member states have hardened demands for protection against Chinese imports that threaten their own industries.

On Monday, Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, agreed a “historic U-turn” on its policy on China by siding with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in authorising effective permission for EU leaders to approve a new instrument to allow them to defend trade by cutting access to the single market at short notice.

In a joint paper with Emmanuel Macron, the two countries spoke of “a massive industrial shock … affecting sectors at the heart of the European industrial model and of systemic relevance [pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive, machine tools, chemicals, etc.]”.

The paper called for the use of all existing trade defence tools, but also for a new diversification instrument and “possible additional” new measures to allow the bloc to react when “third countries seek to undermine the restoration of a level playing field”.

Andrew Small, a former EU adviser on China, said Šefčovič’s talks will test the resolve of both Beijing and Brussels and will “determine whether China is willing to put sufficiently serious offers on the table”.

Small, who is the Asia director at the European Council on Foreign Relations in Berlin, warned: “China’s most effective tactic may be to draw Europe into a ‘process trap’ offering just enough to delay action, without addressing the forces driving European deindustrialisation.”
after newsletter promotion

Sources say the Franco-German proposals for a new instrument, dubbed a “kill switch”, were born out of frustration, particularly in Paris, that a so-called “trade bazooka” available to Brussels, officially known as the anti-coercion instrument, has never been used.
Paris pushed for the use of the ACI following Trump’s threat of tariffs last year but it never gained traction from others as it could take up to a year to implement.

Handlesblatt, the Germany business newspaper, described Monday’s change in policy as “nothing less than an economic turning point”, with chief political reporter Martin Greive concluding in a hard-hitting column that Merz was “putting an end to years of naiveté towards Beijing”.

“Merz has recognised in recent months that Germany is the epicentre of the China shock 2.0; that there might not be much left of German industry if Germany continues to stand by and watch as China gains enormous export advantages through trillions in subsidies, the unilateral siphoning off of knowhow, and a – to put it mildly – questionable monetary policy,” he wrote.

articles.title: Jobless Filipinos drop to 2.77 million in August
articles.summary: The number of jobless Filipinos in August this year declined to 2.77 million, indicating a 5.3% drop in the unemployment rate from July’s 6%.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 11:16am

Individuals flock to the Provincial Training and Development Center II at the Capitol Complex in Lingayen, Pangasinan to apply for jobs offered by various companies at the Labor Day Job Fair on May 1, 2026.
The STAR / Cesar Ramirez
MANILA, Philippines — The number of jobless Filipinos in August this year declined to 2.77 million, indicating a 5.3% drop in the unemployment rate from July’s 6%.

The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported on Wednesday, October 6, that the number of unemployed individuals in the country dropped from July’s 3.14 million but remains higher than the record from the same period last year.
According to the state’s data agency, the unemployment rate in August 2025 stood at 3.9%, or 2.03 million jobless individuals.
National Statistician Claire Dennis Mapa said in a press briefing on Wednesday that the decline was driven by fewer individuals entering the labor force.
“In terms of new entrants, mas konti ngayong pumasok ng August kaysa sa pumasok noong Hulyo,” Mapa said.
(In terms of new entrants, fewer people entered in August than in July.)
Compared with July, when 1.5 million Filipinos entered the labor force, only about 897,000 individuals joined the workforce in August. Of this, 470,000 became employed, while 427,000 were unemployed.
The statistics agency also recorded a higher labor force participation rate in August at 64%, higher than the rate in July, which stood at 63.6%.

The labor force refers to individuals 15 years old and above who are either employed or unemployed. The labor force participation rate in August translates to a total of 52.56 million Filipinos, slightly higher than the 52.36 million in July and the 52.13 million in the same month last year.
Higher employment rate
The employment rate, meanwhile, slightly increased to 94.7% in August compared to July’s 94%.
The rate translates to 49.79 million Filipinos having jobs, which is higher than the 49.21 million recorded in July.
The data agency noted, however, that it is lower than the 96.1% record, or 50.10 million individuals, in August 2025.

Most of the employed individuals came from the services sector, with a 61.7% share, or 30.72 million individuals, followed by the agriculture sector with 20.9%, or 10.43 million people, and the industry sector with 17.3%, or 8.64 million Filipinos.
Bad weather, less work hours. The average weekly working hours of employed individuals in August also went down to around 39.2 hours from around 40.6 hours in July and 41 hours in August 2025.
Mapa said that among the main factors that contributed to the shorter weekly work hours in August were inclement weather conditions and flooding that led to work suspensions.

“Ang malaki talaga na rason ay ‘yung bad weather. So medyo bumaba ‘yung hours worked per week ng mga employed persons dahil ni-reason nila na bad weather and alam natin noong August masyadong maraming araw na malalakas ang ulan at meron tayong pagbaha,” Mapa said.

(The main reason was really bad weather. So, the hours worked per week of employed persons declined because they cited bad weather as the reason, and we know that in August, there were many days of heavy rains and flooding.)

articles.title: Security Council to probe China funds linked to Sara Duterte
articles.summary: National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban Jr. said that the allegations, which emerged during the ongoing impeachment proceedings, may have national security implications.

blocks.text: October 7, 2026 | 11:07am
In this photo uploaded on Facebook on June 26, 2026 shows Vice President Sara Duterte.
Vice President Sara Duterte via Facebook

MANILA, Philippines — The National Security Council (NSC) announced that it will conduct an investigation into reports of foreign financial inflows from China directed toward companies linked to the family of Vice President Sara Duterte.

In a statement on Tuesday, October 6, National Security Adviser Eduardo Oban Jr. said that the allegations, which emerged during the ongoing impeachment proceedings, may have national security implications.

“While the proceedings remain ongoing and the information presented should be properly examined within established legal processes, the reported transactions and any credible information involving significant foreign financial flows that may bear upon the country's national security warrants careful, in-depth, and responsible assessment,” the NSC said.

“The NSC will look into the information presented and, as a matter of policy, continue to task the intelligence and investigative agencies and coordinate with relevant government institutions to assess the national security implications, if any, arising from the reported transactions,” it added.

Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified on Day 33 of the impeachment trial that Cale88 Foods Corp., a firm tied to Vice President Duterte’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, received P319 million in remittances from China and Hong Kong.
Meanwhile, former senator Antonio Trillanes IV alleged during a Friday press briefing that the couple accepted separate payments of P150 million and P319 million through their respective entities.
The Chinese Embassy in Manila denied the allegations, saying that Beijing has never funneled funds to any Philippine political faction.

articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon didn’t talk about Jesse Baird to friend in lead-up to alleged murders, court hears
articles.summary: NSW police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex and Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024 Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Despite an alleged…

blocks.text: Despite an alleged obsession with his ex, Beau Lamarre-Condon never spoke about him to a close friend in the three months before allegedly murdering him, a jury has heard.
Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering his ex-partner Jesse Baird and the man’s new boyfriend Luke Davies in a Sydney terrace in February 2024.

The former senior constable says the two men died in two separate violent struggles with him over his police pistol, and his subsequent efforts to dispose of their bodies were indicative of his panic about the unexpected deaths.
Much evidence in the NSW supreme court trial’s first three weeks has centred on Lamarre-Condon’s alleged growing obsession with Baird in the year leading up to the killings.
The prosecution alleges the then-police officer became infatuated with Baird after they broke off contact in November 2023, resolving to murder him.
However, Lamarre-Condon’s close friend Nicole Harvell told the court on Wednesday she could not remember any conversation with the ex-officer about Baird after the pair broke up for the final time.
That was despite her being in almost daily contact with the now-31-year-old.

blocks.caption: Evidence and testimony in week two of Beau Lamarre-Condon’s trial – video

blocks.text: Harvell, a police senior constable, recalled trying to contact her friend when she saw media reports that he was under suspicion for the two men’s deaths.
“Fuck Beau, are you ok?” she texted to Lamarre-Condon’s phone.
She never received a reply.
The sworn officer maintained under cross-examination that the accused killer had months earlier told her about enlisting his mother to help him lie to Baird.
Lamarre-Condon posted an Instagram story with a bunch of flowers and the caption: “When he’s in Melbourne but still sends you these.”
after newsletter promotion
But publication was restricted to select friends that did not include Baird.
The photo was designed to imply Baird had sent flowers to the accused, despite the pair not being in a relationship at the time, Harvell said.
When Baird discovered the ruse, Lamarre-Condon spent $160 on a bouquet identical to the photo to lie to him, the officer’s friend said.
Lamarre-Condon then sent a photo to Baird showing his mother with the fresh bouquet.
The bouquet had a handwritten note to imply his mother had been the intended recipient and they were from her partner, who was in Melbourne, the jury heard.
“I recall the accused telling me his mother had written that note,” Harvell said.
The trial continues.

articles.title: Mali: Junta forces retake strategic town of Kidal from separatists
articles.summary: Mali's military regained control of the strategic town of Kidal after forcing Tuareg separatists and al Queda-linked jihadists to withdraw following an offensive backed by Russia's Africa Corps.

image.caption: Malian troops ⁠were "reinforcing ⁠their presence" in the town by Tuesday night, a government statement said [FILE: May 9, 2026]Image: AFP

blocks.text: Mali's army, supported by Russian paramilitary forces, has re-entered the northern town of Kidal, forcing the Tuareg separatists to withdraw from the strategic hold, in a symbolic boost for the country's military government and its Russian allies.

The Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) said in a statement it had "decided to carry out a strategic and controlled withdrawal of its forces from the town of Kidal." It said the withdrawal took place without direct fighting.
This followed the "disproportionate use of aerial assets by Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps," according to an FLA spokesperson.
How did Kidal fall earlier this year?
The FLA and al-Qaeda-linked Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) seized Kidal during a series of attacks earlier this year in April that also killed Mali's defense minister.
Tuareg separatists from the Azawad Liberation Front have been fighting for years to create an independent state in northern Mali.
Mali's junta, which came to power in back-to-back coups in 2020 and 2021, has increasingly relied on Russian paramilitary support against fighters linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State.

blocks.caption: Mali's junta in recent years distanced itself from former colonial power France and deepened military and political ties with Russia [FILE: May 9, 2026]Image: AFP

blocks.text: What does Kidal's recapture mean for Mali's junta?
Analysts say the latest advance is largely a symbolic victory for Mali's junta.

"A successful recapture... affirms the military-led government's authority and boosts the army's morale, particularly after several high-profile setbacks both in the north and the central regions in recent weeks," Beverly Ochieng, associate director of Control Risks, told Reuters.
Ochieng, however, added the retaking of Kidal is largely "symbolic" and not "decisive" in Mali's campaign against jihadist and separatist groups.
Human rights organizations have often accused the Malian army and Russian paramilitaries of killing civilians during military operations, with all sides also accused of committing war crimes.

articles.title: Football: Lionel Messi plays final game for Argentina
articles.summary: Argentinian superstar Lionel Messi bowed out of international football with one last goal for his country. For football in Argentina, and indeed across the world, it's the end of an era.

image.caption: Argentinian fans have long worshipped Messi as the successor to the great Diego MaradonaImage: Gustavo Garello/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Lionel Messi made his 208th and final appearance for Argentina on Tuesday night, scoring his 126th and final international goal as the Albiceleste beat Benin 3-0 in a friendly in Buenos Aires.
In emotional scenes at a packed El Monumental stadium, Messi stepped up to convert a penalty in the 71st minute, prompting wild celebrations from teammates and fans alike.

Earlier, the 39-year-old superstar had already set up goals for teammates Nicolas Otamendi – who was also making his final appearance for the national team – and Nico Paz – the youngster who is widely tipped to inherit Messi's iconic number 10 jersey.

"It was a source of great pride for me to wear this jersey," Messi told fans in an address after the final whistle. "I can only express my gratitude... not coming back anymore will be deeply painful."
"Gracias, Leo!" read an intricate drone show in the sky above the stadium at full-time, which concluded with the drones forming a profile of Messi's face.

blocks.caption: Messi (left) also set up a goal for Nicolas Otamendi (19), who was also making his final appearance for ArgentinaImage: Matias Baglietto/REUTERS

blocks.text: Messi: 'Proud to be Argentinian'
Widely considered the best player of all time, Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31 – barely a month after Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the World Cup final.
"It was a decision which hurts and still hurts but I know it's the right time," he wrote in a statement composed just two days after the defeat in East Rutherford, USA.
"I swear that I have always given everything and that I have always fought for this shirt to make you happy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football," he said.
"Thank you, God for making me Argentinian."
Messi: following in the footsteps of Maradona

Argentina may have lost the 2026 World Cup final, but Messi's crowning moment came four years earlier when he led his nation to glory in Qatar, beating France on penalties after a spectacular final had ended 3-3.

The triumph crowned an international career which hadn't always been easy as Messi, so prolific in club football for Barcelona, struggled to live up to expectations in his home country, where fans worshipped him as the successor to the great Diego Maradona.

He announced his international retirement once before in 2016 after losing three consecutive finals with Argentina – the 2014 World Cup final vs. Germany in Brazil and the 2015 and 2016 Copa America finals, both to Chile.
But he reversed his decision and led his country to the Copa America title in 2021, ending Argentina's 28-year wait for a trophy, before finally winning the World Cup in 2022.
Messi may have retired from international football, but he still has a contract with his current club, Major League Soccer (MLS) side Inter Miami, until 2028.

articles.title: Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation
articles.summary:
Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen

Three friends of

blocks.text: Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit.
“Arrest them immediately!! Like yesterday,” Owens captioned the post.

In a Monday complaint filed in a Mississippi district court, the fathers of the three young men, who are also named in the complaint as plaintiffs because they are deemed minors under state law, accuse Owens of harming their reputation and endangering their physical safety with the post.

“Due to the conduct of Owens and many other less-famous individuals, these completely innocent young men have been subjected to thousands of death threats, face-to-face harassment, and daily fear and ridicule from complete strangers. They’ve even been refused service at public establishments. Their lives, and the lives of their family members, will never be the same,” the complaint alleges.
Owens could not be immediately reached for comment.
The friends’ counsel also indicated they intend to take legal action against other public figures who have been vocal about Wells’s death including Al Sharpton and The View’s Sunny Hostin.
On 4 July, Wells and his friends sailed for a Mississippi island. He was last seen that afternoon. Two days later, his body was found on the island.

The circumstances of his death have fueled public suspicion. Wells, who was African American, had been partying with a mostly white friend group – a detail that gained traction online as some referenced Mississippi’s past with racial violence.

In late September, a Mississippi grand jury declined to file criminal charges, finding Wells’s death to appear “consistent with drowning”. Jackson county district attorney Angel Myers McIlrath has said Wells’s death was not racially motivated.

Wells’s parents and civil rights lawyer Ben Crump continue to call for further investigations, citing the state’s autopsy report, which said Wells’s airways and stomach were empty. His family has said the lack of water found undermines the drowning determination.

“I cannot take that ruling, and I cannot move on with my life,” Christine Wonsley, Wells’s mother, reportedly said, referring to the grand jury’s findings at a Monday press conference. “We have been left with more questions and heartbreak than any answers.”

articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.

image.caption: U.S. President Donald Trump, left, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are seen in Alaska in August 2025. (Jae C. Hong/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute.
WHO says Siberia case presents a 'very low' risk outside Russia

Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he would be talking with Putin about the case "very soon." Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause.

Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in "very deep discussions" on the topic. "We'll be able to report about it, probably tomorrow," Trump said.

The World Health Organization on Tuesday said the case presents a "very low" risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East.
On Monday, Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation.
What we know about the suspected plague death in Russia

The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18.

articles.title: ‘Not exactly his favorite senator’: Susan Collins distances herself from Trump in Maine debate
articles.summary:
Republican challenged by Democrat Troy Jackson in critical Senate race says she opposes Iran war and Canada tariffs

Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced…

blocks.text: Susan Collins, the Republican senator for Maine, pointedly distanced herself from Donald Trump in a televised debate with Democratic challenger Troy Jackson on Tuesday, as she sought to present an image of independence in a state that has voted against Trump three times.

Proclaiming herself as not the US president’s “favorite senator”, Collins made the highly unusual boast for a Republican that she had voted with Joe Biden, a Democrat, more than 90% of the time when he was president. She also emphasized her differences with her fellow Republicans, saying she voted against her own party more than any other senator.

Collins’ defensiveness came amid a determined onslaught from Jackson, 58, a veteran former state legislator who was getting his first chance to present himself to a broad audience since replacing Graham Platner as the Democratic candidate in a contest that could be vital to the party’s hopes of winning the Senate.

Platner, a former harbor master, was forced to withdraw from the race in July after facing sexual assault allegations, which he denied, leaving Democrats racing against the clock to replace a candidate who had built up momentum campaigning on a populist progressive platform.

Jackson painted Collins as a Trump loyalist, saying she voted with the president 96% of the time. He also doggedly focused on her 2018 vote for the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh, tying it to the court’s subsequent overturning of Roe v Wade, which had for half a century guaranteed the national right to abortion.

“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in a pithy opening statement. “Eight years ago today, Maine women went to DC and begged Senator Collins not to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, but she did it anyways.
“He helped overturn Roe v Wade, and today she says she has no regrets. Would you trust her to pick the next supreme court justice?”

Collins, 73, who has been a senator since 1996, has frequently presented herself as a moderate who stands against more radical trends in her own party. The posture is in line with Maine’s profile as a more Democratic-leaning state, which Trump has not won in any of his three presidential campaigns and which has voted for Democrat presidential candidates in every election since 1992.

Nevertheless, Collins went to unusual lengths to differentiate herself from Trump on a range of issues, including the war with Iran, which she said she voted to end nine times, calling it “not well thought out”.
Collins reacted with something close to alarm when the moderator, Gregg Lagerquist, said Trump had suggested that the president might pay a campaign visit to Maine.

“I don’t think that President Trump is going to come to Maine,” she said. “He’s talking about going to a lot of different states. I’ve heard nothing from his office, and I’m not exactly his favorite senator.”
Collins stressed her differences with the president on specific issues pertinent to the Maine economy, including rural healthcare and tariffs against Canada, with which the state shares a border.
“I have been the most outspoken opponent of the tariffs on Canada,” she said. “Canada is not China. It’s our neighbor and our friends.”
Polls show the two candidates running neck and neck.

blocks.text: Rep. Leandro Leviste (Batangas, 1st District) holds a press conference on Wednesday, Nov. 19, 2025.
Leandro Leviste via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — A Makati Regional Trial Court (RTC) has issued a warrant of arrest against Rep. Leandro Leviste (Batangas 1st District) over alleged violations of the Public Service Act.
According to a copy of the warrant of arrest sent to reporters by the National Bureau of Investigation, the Makati RTC Branch 235 issued the warrant on October 5.

“You are hereby commanded to arrest LEANDRO ANTONIO L. LEVISTE, who is/are said to be found in/at N/A, PARAISO, CALATAGAN, BATANGAS, CALABARZON or elsewhere, and who has/have been charged before me with the offense of PUBLIC SERVICE ACT SECTION 25 OF COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 146, AS AMENDED BY RA NO. 11659) and bring him/her/them forthwith before me to be dealt with according to law,” a portion of the warrant of arrest read.
The Makati court has set Leviste’s bail at P72,000.

This is part of the graft and plunder case being investigated by the Office of the Ombudsman against Leviste and his mother, Sen. Loren Legarda, over alleged irregularities involving solar energy projects and service contracts linked to Leviste’s companies.

articles.title: David Ellison denies he has ‘politicized’ Skydance despite close Trump links
articles.summary: Ellison admits ‘good relationship’ with administration in remarks to reporters about newly merged media company David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance,…

blocks.text: David Ellison, the chief executive of the newly formed media conglomerate Skydance, denied that he has “politicized” the company despite the close connection he has forged with Donald Trump’s White House over the 20 months of his administration.

“We have a good relationship with this administration,” Ellison acknowledged to reporters at a Tuesday press briefing focused on the now-consummated merger of Paramount Skydance and CNN parent company Warner Bros Discovery.

“I also had a really good relationship with President Biden. I have a good relationship with [Republican South Carolina senator] Tim Scott, and I have a good relationship with Governor Gavin Newsom. I think it is important to talk to everybody on both sides of the aisle … When you’re operating within a business-friendly administration, you should always have those relationships.”
“We want to speak to everybody,” Ellison added. “We do not want to politicize the company.”

Asked about his conversations with Trump about CNN, Ellison did not directly discuss his communications with the president, the network’s most prominent critic. But he said he wanted to clarify that “we have not talked to any political leader of any party about news, other than to say that we want to be in the truth business and we want to be in the trust business. And we believe in complete editorial independence.”

Amid concerns about whether Ellison might move CNN in a more rightward editorial direction, he said that both the cable news network and CBS News would be “completely editorially independent”, echoing a message he delivered earlier in the day during a town hall meeting with company employees.

Ellison also gave an endorsement to the two leaders he has tapped to continue running the two news networks networks he now controls, CNN chief executive Mark Thompson and CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.
On Monday, Thompson told staffers in a memo that he would remain at the merged company, while Skydance also confirmed that Weiss would remain in her role.
“We’re thrilled, obviously, with Mark,” Ellison said. “We’re thrilled with Bari.”

Asked about a potential merging of CBS News and CNN and any cuts – or “synergies” – that might stem from that, Ellison said he and his leadership team would spend the next several months “basically getting under the hood on all of that”. Most of the $6bn in expected savings from the merger would not come from job losses, he said.
Ellison was not asked about Weiss’s performance as the editorial leader of CBS News. When asked specifically about Weiss’s performance by a Guardian reporter in June, Ellison ignored the question.

articles.title: Palace rejects VP Sara's claim that Marcos admin was behind cash delivery claims
articles.summary: “Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan."

blocks.text: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. and Vice President Sara Duterte on January 25, 2024.
STAR / KJ Rosales

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang dismissed Vice President Sara Duterte’s claims that the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was behind the multi-million-peso cash delivery allegations against her to undermine her reputation.
“Wala nang masisira kay VP Sara; nasa katawan na niya ‘yan,” Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said in an interview on Tuesday, October 6, when asked to react to Duterte’s allegations.
(There’s nothing left to tarnish about Vice President Sara; it’s already on her.)

Earlier Tuesday, Duterte accused the Marcos administration and its communications officials of orchestrating efforts to damage her reputation and redirecting the president’s corruption issues toward her.
This came after dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. claimed that more than P2 billion in cash was delivered to her upon the instructions of former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Duterte denied the allegations anew and reiterated that she did not personally know Gracioso.
Pointing fingers
Castro said the vice president is just pointing fingers at others because she can no longer present valid evidence to debunk the allegations.
“Siguro ‘yun talaga ‘yung mangyayari kapag ka wala nang mahanap na pang-defense, magtuturo ka na lang ng iba. Wala pang naibibigay na ebidensiya na wala silang natanggap,” Castro said.
(Perhaps that’s what happens when you can’t find anything to defend yourself, you’ll point to others. No evidence has been presented to prove that they received nothing.)

The Palace spokesperson also answered Duterte’s claims that Gracioso’s statements are intended to support the alleged unexplained wealth allegations against her in the ongoing impeachment trial, saying that the vice president has failed to properly deny the allegations against her.
“So ang pangulo, lagi niyang itinuturo. Hindi kayang ibenta ng pangulo ang bansa sa dayuhan. Isa itong karumal-dumal na gawain, so ‘wag natin itong tularan,” Castro said.
(She’s always pointing to the president. The president cannot sell the country to foreigners. It’s a heinous act, so let’s not follow this.)

articles.title: Chinese state firm among entities that sent P319 million to Duterte-linked company — Hontiveros
articles.summary: A Chinese state-owned enterprise with direct ties to the Chinese Communist Party and Beijing’s foreign influence apparatus was among the entities that remitted millions of pesos to Calle88…

blocks.text: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte gestures as she leaves the Hall of Justice in Quezon City, Metro Manila on Sept. 11, 2026.
AFP / Jam Sta Rosa

MANILA, Philippines — A Chinese state-owned enterprise with direct ties to the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Beijing’s foreign influence apparatus was among the entities that remitted millions of pesos to Calle88 Foods Corp., a company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte.
During the impeachment trial on October 6, Sen. Risa Hontiveros revealed that her office’s research uncovered deep geopolitical links behind the P319 million that entered Calle88 from China.
The Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) had previously flagged these transactions as covered and suspicious transaction reports due to a lack of legitimate underlying transactions.
According to Hontiveros, one of the entities that sent money to Calle88 is China National Township Enterprises.

“Base po sa research ng opisina ko, dating directly under the Ministry of Agriculture sa China at naging isang large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council,” Hontiveros said.

(Based on my office’s research, it was previously directly under the Ministry of Agriculture in China and became a large state-owned agricultural enterprise under the supervision of the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council.)
She added that the public profiles of China National Township Enterprises openly mention being "committed to serving the implementation of the country's Belt and Road Initiative and foreign policy.”

Another enterprise mentioned by Hontiveros was Beijing Jianweifang Food Co., owned by the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group, which acts as its Series A investor and has maintained a strategic cooperation agreement with the Beijing firm since 2019.
She said that the Xinjiang Fruit Industry Group is "not an ordinary company" but a Chinese state-owned enterprise that actively advances the interests of the CCP.

“It's a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Sa mismong corporate governance structure ng Xinjiang Fruit may institutional Chinese Communist Party organization na naka-embed,” Hontiveros said.

(It is a Chinese state-owned enterprise. It advances the interests of the Chinese Communist Party. Embedded within the very corporate governance structure of Xinjiang Fruit is an institutional Chinese Communist Party organization.)

When asked by Hontiveros whether the AMLC is actively investigating these Chinese companies and their geopolitical linkages, AMLC Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura said that he was unable to answer.
“The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed po 'yung pong mga na-submit po namin na…Summary report po, financial investigation report, financial investigation report,” Buenaventura said.
(The only documents related to what we were subpoenaed for are the ones we submitted, which are the summary report and the financial investigation reports.)
In a statement on October 5, the Chinese Embassy denied that Beijing had ties to a "Philippine political faction."
Calle88 was listed among the business interests connected with Sara Duterte in her 2022–2025 Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.
However, records from the Securities and Exchange Commission show that Duterte’s husband, Manases Carpio, was an incorporator, director and shareholder of Calle88 from 2021 to 2024.
His ownership reportedly reached 47.5% in 2024, but his name no longer appeared as a shareholder in 2025.
Editor's note: This story has been updated to clarify that China National Township Enterprises was one of the entities that remitted money to Calle88 Foods Corp.

articles.title: Christa Pike awake after failed Tennessee execution: lawyers
articles.summary: A death row inmate who survived a botched execution last week is conscious and talking in hospital, according to her lawyers, who want to commute her death sentence to life imprisonment without…

image.caption: Christa Pike was transported from prison to hospital after last week's botched executionImage: George Walker IV/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: A prisoner who survived an attempt to carry out the death penalty in Tennessee, the United States, last week is conscious and speaking as she continues to receive treatment in hospital.
"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," the inmate's attorneys said in a statement on Tuesday.
"Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented."

Pike, who was sentenced to death for the beating, stabbing and murder of a classmate in 1995, survived two doses of the lethal injection drug pentobarbital – which her lawyers said left her arms burned and blistered.
Christa Pike not 'free of further serious risk'
"She's still in the ICU," said Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta in neighboring Georgia, who consulted as an expert for Pike's legal team.

"She has recovered to a certain degree that she's able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk. There's still a lot of bad things that can happen here, even when everyone is doing their job well."
Tuesday's updates were the first indication that Pike's condition has improved since the failed execution attempt at a Nashville prison last Wednesday.

Her attorneys thanked first responders and medical staff who they said have "treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her" – as they prepare to go to court on Wednesday seeking to learn more about what went wrong with the lethal injection.

blocks.caption: Christa Pike was sentenced to death on March 30, 1996 for her role as a teenager in the torture-murder of her 19-year-old schoolmateImage: WBIR-TV/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Pike's attorneys seeking to commute sentence
The lawyers are seeking a court order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence, including drug lot numbers, records and other information from the attempted execution.
Ultimately, they are looking to have Pike's sentence commuted to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
While Dr. Zivot said Pike's current state "bodes well for a good recovery," her attorneys warned that her prognosis is still "unclear" and said she faces "a long recovery."
"Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time," they said.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, which publishes data and analysis on capital punishment in the United States, Pike is the first prisoner ever to survive "after being injected with lethal doses of execution drugs."

articles.title: New Zealand greenhouse gas levels hit record highs threatening catastrophic glacier melts
articles.summary:
Government report finds the country could be hit with more frequent and intense heatwaves, as well as damaging storms and cyclones

New Zealand could be hit with more frequent and intense…

blocks.text: New Zealand could be hit with more frequent and intense heatwaves and catastrophic glacier melts in the near future, as greenhouse gas levels hit record highs, a new report about the nation’s climate has revealed.

Released on Wednesday, the Our Atmosphere and Climate 2026 report shows New Zealand is experiencing mounting climate pressures, which will have wide-reaching implications for the environment, native species and communities.

“The signal is just becoming clearer … there are multiple indicators that are showing increased warming and the likelihood of climate change,” Dr Alison Collins, chief science adviser for the ministry for cities, environment, regions and transport (Mcert) told the Guardian.
New Zealand’s annual average temperature has risen by 1.36C since records began in 1909, and seven of the 10 warmest years on record occurred in the last decade, the report said.
“Whilst it sounds like a small amount … it is a significant baseline shift that’s having ramifications through nature, through our communities, and through businesses and industry,” Collins said.

The report finds that as the climate heats, glaciers are shrinking. New Zealand has roughly 3000 glaciers, and they have shrunk in volume from 56 cubic kilometres in 1997 to 30 cubic kilometres in 2023, the report said.

Modelling of glacier retreat shows a high risk of further decline on the horizon. Under the “low climate scenario” – which assumes low emissions – glaciers will very likely lose between 14 and 86% of their volume by 2100. Under the “high climate scenario”, that figure rises to between 69 and 100% of their volume.
“We’re talking about substantial loss,” Collins said.

blocks.caption: Flooding caused by Cyclone Gabrielle in Awatoto, near the city of Napier.  Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Greenhouse gases have increased to record levels in New Zealand’s atmosphere, the report shows. There was a 30% increase in carbon dioxide since monitoring began in New Zealand in 1972. Methane levels had also slightly increased in 2025 to their highest concentration ever.
“That additional heat is showing up in rising temperatures, warming oceans, rising seas, shifting rainfall patterns and more intense extremes,” the report said.

Among those extremes were heatwaves, which the report said were “very likely” to increase in frequency, length and intensity across the country. The number of days hitting more than 25C was also “very likely” to increase by 2050, which will expose people to heat-related health risks, including physical illness, disease and psychological distress.

Marine heatwaves are also becoming more pronounced and affecting some native species, the report said. In 2025, the series revealed New Zealand’s oceans were warming 34% faster than the global average which has been linked to mass sea sponge bleaching, die-offs of southern bull kelp, large scale fish standings and penguin deaths.

The three-yearly update from Mcert and Stats NZ collates statistics, data and research across five domains – air, atmosphere and climate, freshwater, land, and marine – to paint a picture of the state of New Zealand’s environment.

The report outlined a myriad of issues that will stem from continued warming, including damaging storms and cyclones that pose a risk to life, droughts affecting species and agricultural industries, sea level rise eroding infrastructure and housing and Māori communities having reduced access to culturally significant places.
Severe storms, including Cyclone Gabrielle and the Auckland floods in 2023, have battered New Zealand in recent years, causing deaths, widespread devastation and billions of dollars in costs.
New Zealand was built and developed around a relatively stable set of climate conditions and the report examines what happens when those conditions begin to change, Collins said.
“Climate change is not just an environmental issue. It’s a human story. It’s an economic story.”

articles.title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows
articles.summary: A sharp increase in human activity is affecting the way the Himalayan monal lives and communicates, studies show.

blocks.text: A sharp increase in human activity is having an impact on the way a Himalayan bird lives and communicates, two studies by Indian researchers have found.

The monal, a pheasant native to Himalayan mountain forests, is deeply woven into the region's cultural, folklore and identity. The eye-catching monal - the male has distinctive green, blue and copper feathers - is the state bird of India's Uttarakhand state and the national bird of Nepal, reflecting its cultural significance across the Himalayas.
But studies show that infrastructure development and tourism are squeezing its habitat, while increasing noise is altering how it communicates with potential mates and rivals.
Researchers from Uttarakhand conducted two separate studies over five years which flagged key threats to the bird.

One study found that the birds are forced to move higher in the mountains as their natural habitat in the alpine meadows above the tree line get crowded. The other says the monal is changing its pitch to cut through human noise in a busy valley.

"These two studies give a useful warning for other more vulnerable species - if the monal is forced to change both its voice and its address, how are the more sensitive species responding?" says Vishal Singh, an environmental practitioner working on ecology and climate issues in the Himalayas.

Dr Rajeev Lochan, lead researcher of both studies, told the BBC that they chose to study the monal as the bird has a narrow habitat range - it moves seasonally between the lower montane zone - an ecological belt found on the lower slopes of the mountains - and high-elevation alpine zones. This, he says, makes it a key indicator of ecosystem health in the north-western Himalayas.
"If the species is facing issues on this particular landscape, there might be a chance that the ecological disturbances are affecting other birds too," said Lochan.
The monal, researchers say, can be seen as a stand-in for the health of a fragile Himalayan ecosystem pushed to a tipping point due to unregulated tourism and heavy urbanisation.

While the region has always drawn tourists, trekkers and researchers given its scenic landscape and biodiversity, rapid infrastructure expansion in the past decade has made more places accessible, increasing footfall and disrupting the wildlife. This, coupled with mounting human pressures, suggests that climate change is emerging as another major threat to the region's already vulnerable biodiversity.
"There are a lot of factors at play but at a broader level, the problem is that the economic development of the region is not aligned to its ecological integrity," Singh said.

items: The Himalayas are melting faster - and India's economy is 'at risk'
Why the mighty Himalayas are getting harder and harder to see

blocks.text: According to the first study, climate change is projected to continue shrinking and destabilising the Himalayan monal's habitat across the Indian Himalayas through 2100 under multiple climate scenarios.
Currently, the birds are found in alpine meadows, located high in the mountains above the forests, which form some of the Himalayas' most important seasonal grazing and biodiversity-rich habitats.

The researchers modelled how climate change could shift the monal's suitable habitat across the Indian Himalayan region in the states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. It was based on the kind of global climate models and emissions scenarios used for assessments by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the UN's climate science unit.

"These birds are now slowly moving upwards in the Himalayas as the snow is melting and vegetation is growing, making the area accessible to them. They are anyway being pushed upwards as their natural habitats in alpine meadows are being encroached upon by humans," Lochan said.
The model assumes that the bird needs the current climate set-up that exists in alpine meadows in the future too, a reasonable but not certain assumption.

The birds' seasonal migration may become increasingly difficult as changes in climate may force them to move to higher elevations on hills, to smaller and fragmented areas. Their population would be scattered in disconnected pockets, which reduces chances of breeding between groups and increases their risks of long-term decline or local extinction, which is already a threat, the study says.

The second study, also conducted by Lochan, Dinesh Kumar Sharma and Anand Kumar, who work at the Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, focuses on the bird's behavioural changes. They conducted the study in two valleys in Kedarnath Musk Deer Sanctuary in Uttarakhand - at Chopta, a tourist spot with busy traffic and visitors, and the largely quiet Madmaheshwar.
They recorded more than 700 monal calls across both sites using microphones and passive recording devices and then measured pitch, call length and background noise levels for a year from April 2023.
Birds in noisy environments consistently produced calls with significantly higher peak frequencies compared with those in quieter habitats, the study said.
The researchers found subtle changes in the monal's pitch that could be picked up by recording devices but might go unnoticed by the human ear.

"This does not mean that the species has undergone a permanent or evolutionary change in its vocal frequency; rather, our findings suggest behavioural flexibility in response to different acoustic environments," Lochan said.
Compared with the birds in Madmaheshwar valley, the monal in Chopta also produced shorter call durations likely to cut through low-frequency human noise from traffic and tourist footfall.
Bird calls are one of the most sophisticated forms of sound-based communication in the natural world, and significant changes can interfere with, among other things, their mating success.

"When a species must raise its pitch to be heard over tourist traffic, or climb higher as meadows turn crowded, it reveals how human pressure is rewriting the rules of life in the Himalaya," says Anjal Prakash, a public policy professor at FLAME University and contributor to IPCC reports.
Lochan says he and his team consider this a preliminary study and hope to expand the scope and depth of it.

The research comes with the caveat that it is not conclusive on ecological consequences, and more research is needed. But together, the two studies signal broader ecological stress across the Himalayas.
"In listening to the monal, we hear the Himalayas asking for space, silence and care," says Prakash.

articles.title: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar-winning On the Waterfront actor, dead at 102
articles.summary: Eva Marie Saint, the pale, willowy actor who won an Academy Award for her first movie, On the Waterfront, and starred opposite Cary Grant in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller North by Northwest, has…

image.caption: U.S. actor Eva Marie Saint, in the U.K. in 1966. Saint, the pale, willowy actor who won an Academy Award for her first movie, On the Waterfront, and starred opposite Cary Grant in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller North by Northwest, has died. She was 102. (Evening Standard/Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

Eva Marie Saint, the pale, willowy actor who won an Academy Award for her first movie, On the Waterfront, and starred opposite Cary Grant in the Alfred Hitchcock thriller North by Northwest, has died. She was 102.
Hollywood star also featured opposite Cary Grant in North by Northwest
Saint, whose acting work lasted well into her 90s, died at her home in Los Angeles on Tuesday, confirmed family representative Jeff Sanderson.

Saint had one of the most spectacular debuts in Hollywood history as the love interest of Marlon Brando's tormented Terry Malloy in On the Waterfront, and her first trip to the Academy Awards was memorable, too. Pregnant with her first child, Saint accepted her Oscar from Frank Sinatra and smilingly murmured a unique winner's speech: "I think I may have the baby right here." (Her son, Darrell, was born two days later.)

The award for the 1954 classic made her an instant star, but she soon astonished Hollywood with a firm independence that would mark her career. She refused offers of studio contracts and declined chances to follow up on her great success, explaining that she was taking time off to become acquainted with her new son. (A daughter, Laurette, was born in 1958.)

In her first decade in Hollywood, Saint appeared in a mere seven films. She declined such top-level productions as The Man in the Gray Flannel Suit with Gregory Peck, Summer and Smoke with Laurence Harvey and The Rainmaker with Burt Lancaster. She credited her husband, TV and stage director Jeffrey Hayden, with persuading her to star in Hitchcock's North by Northwest, the classic 1959 thriller in which Saint plays a spy who seduces Grant's character, but ends up falling for him.
In her first decade in Hollywood, Saint appeared in a mere seven films. (Keystone Features/Getty Images)

"I vividly remember him saying, 'Honey, I think you should find a quiet spot. I'll take care of the children and I want you to really think about this and reread this script,"' she told Vanity Fair in 2014. "He was so right. And that's what husbands are for."

Instead of being put off by her selectivity, studios continued offering her starring roles in such films as Exodus (with Newman), Raintree County (with Elizabeth Taylor and Montgomery Clift) and All Fall Down, with Warren Beatty.

items: Jeffrey Hayden, veteran TV & stage director, dead at 90

blocks.text: She turned more to television in the 1970s and enjoyed renewed popularity in the 1980s as the mother of Cybill Shepherd in the hit sitcom Moonlighting and as Tom Hanks's mother in the comedy film Nothing in Common. She won an Emmy for the 1990 miniseries People Like Us, and had roles in such 21st-century movies as Because of Winn-Dixie, Superman Returns and Winter's Tale, the latter of which was adapted from Mark Helprin's novel of the same name. In 2021, she played Marisa Tomei's aunt in the brief audio play The Bus Ride, part of The Pack Podcast.
Saint was married to Hayden for 55 years, until his death in 2016.
Saint, left, and husband, Jeffrey Hayden, attend an event in Los Angeles in October 1957. Saint was married to Hayden for 55 years, until his death in 2016. (Harold P. Matosian/The Associated Press)

When Saint emerged in the public consciousness, many believed her theatrical-sounding name must have been invented. She was born with it on July 4, 1924, in Newark, N.J. The family moved to Delmar, a small town near Albany, N.Y., where her father was a Goodrich Rubber Co. manager. Saint's goal was to become a third-grade teacher like her mother, but at Bowling Green State University in Ohio she tried out for a play and won the leading role.

After graduation she lived with her parents in Flushing, Long Island, and began hunting for acting jobs in Manhattan. After a fruitless year, she landed a two-line role as a telephone operator on a radio drama and soon was working steadily on soap operas and nighttime dramas, appearing for two years as Claudia on One Man's Family. Network television was booming in the early 1950s, and her looks and dramatic sense made her a favourite with casting people and producers.

A critical turn in Saint's career came when she auditioned before Elia Kazan and was accepted into the Actors Studio, which shaped a generation of method-actor stars. She credited acting coach Lee Strasberg with helping her overcome her shyness.
PHOTOS | Eva Marie Saint and some of her roles:

"Lee Strasberg, when he got to know me a little bit, gave me a scene to do where I had to cry in front of my peers," she told the Santa Barbara Independent in 2009. "I worried about it, I worked on it, I tried to use what I was learning at the studio. I finally did the scene, and I cried, and my peers were crying with me. It was just an incredible moment for me."

Saint was rejected for the single female role in the play Mister Roberts, but was hired to understudy the actor chosen, Jocelyn Brando, Marlon's sister. In six frustrating months, Saint never got to substitute for Brando. She finally made it to Broadway in A Trip to Bountiful, which she had played on television.

Kazan invited her to try out for the female lead in On the Waterfront by improvising a scene with Marlon Brando. She was told to try to stop a young man from entering her apartment. She told the Los Angeles Times in 2001: "All I know is that Marlon got in the door and turned on the music. We started dancing. He flicked my skirt. Kazan saw the sparks fly, and that's how I got the part."

articles.title: Many Nepalis swept away in the floods aren't officially dead, leaving families in limbo
articles.summary: Relatives are finding themselves with no compensation and facing an administrative nightmare.

blocks.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images
In Hindu tradition, when a body cannot be recovered, a symbolic effigy is made from sacred "kusha" grass to represent the dead
ByAzadeh Moshiri
South Asia correspondent

At the Pashupatinath temple, on the banks of the Bagmati River in Kathmandu, Madan Lal Lawat joined other families in honouring loved ones who were lost when a deadly flood tore through the China-Nepal border last month.
In Hindu tradition, when a body cannot be recovered, a symbolic effigy is made from sacred "kusha" grass to represent the dead, allowing relatives to perform last rites.
With more than 5,000 people still missing and the government ending rescue operations, this is the only way people like Lawat can honour the dead.
Five of his relatives - including his brother - were caught in the water's onslaught and are still missing. Lawat survived because he was driving his bus outside his village, Betrawati.
The last Lawat heard from survivors is that his brother Mangal died while going door-to-door, trying to warn others to leave.
"I don't know how to start over. Police say they're still searching for the bodies, but I'm not sure they'll ever be found," Lawat says.
He has little doubt they are dead.
But legally, their fate is far more complicated. In Nepal, a missing person is only presumed dead after 12 years.

blocks.caption: Image caption, The last Madan Lal Lawat heard from survivors is that his brother Mangal (pictured) died while going door-to-door, trying to warn others to leave

blocks.text: Image source, Supplied
The last Madan Lal Lawat heard from survivors is that his brother Mangal (pictured) died while going door-to-door, trying to warn others to leave
Section 40 of Nepal's Civil Code does allow for some exceptions, but it does not have a provision for disasters like the flood witnessed last month.
Families like Lawat's have told the BBC they are struggling to obtain death certificates, affecting everything from accessing flood compensation to the transfer of properties and even inheritance.

Relatives can receive up to 25,000 rupees (£122; $162) for funeral costs, in addition to about 200,000 rupees (£981; $1,302) in bereavement compensation for the first relative who died, and 100,000 rupees (£491; $651) for each additional death.
But this is only possible once they submit a death certificate. So as families try to rebuild their lives, many are now caught in an administrative nightmare.
"In view of the current disaster, the law is outdated," says constitutional law expert, Bipin Adhikari.

He explains the law was meant to account for people who travelled abroad and weren't heard from for years. "But technology has advanced now, it isn't as difficult to send or receive information," he argues.
For Lawat, the legal minefield has made an already devastating loss even harder to navigate.

When he tried to obtain a death certificate last week, officials at the local municipality office turned him away. "They said they're still discussing the death certificate issue. We aren't sure what to do now. There's so much uncertainty," he tells us.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Most of Betrawati village was swallowed up in the floods

blocks.text: Most of Betrawati village was swallowed up in the floods

Even when bodies are recovered, identifying their identities is a slow and challenging task. More than 1,400 bodies have been recovered so far, and Nepal has little experience in processing DNA at such scale. In some cases, authorities have taken DNA samples, then buried the bodies with markers in the ground, should families claim them.
Given the scale of damage and loss, families say compensation is desperately needed.
Nepal's latest assessment counts 7,570 private buildings damaged or destroyed, home to nearly 33,000 people based on census data.

The BBC visited Lawat's village Betrawati just days after the disaster, once the roads to the district of Rasuwa had been cleared. For days, this area had been cut off from the capital Kathmandu, and struggling with a shortage of basic supplies including petrol.

The damage in the village was staggering. The ground was nothing but hardened mud and silt. Footage of the flood showed it had swallowed most of the village in just minutes. There was no sign of its bustling market, the local Uttargaya School was in ruins, the houses swept away, and school buses were turned over.

Betrawati straddles flood-devastated Rasuwa and Nuwakot, and is part of the Bidur municipality, where the government estimates more than 3,000 buildings have been damaged or destroyed. It's the largest amount of any municipality.
Local governments are now urging the prime minister's office to figure out a way to resolve the death confirmation issue.
"Everything is on hold," Bidur's Mayor, Rajan Shrestha, told the BBC.
He said it could take up to 12 years for relatives to access the funds they are entitled to.
For one of South Asia's smallest economies, finding money for compensation is a challenge, and the sums on offer are small when compared with the scale of the losses.

blocks.caption: Image caption, More than 5,000 people are still missing after the floods, leaving families stricken with grief

blocks.text: More than 5,000 people are still missing after the floods, leaving families stricken with grief
The government puts damage to personal belongings alone at £123 million ($165 million) across more than 8,300 households.
This implies losses of about £14,800 ($20,000) on average per household, though this figure is only based on census data and modelling, and doesn't represent the exact cost per family.
The financial toll makes the death certificates vital for families trying to recover from the disaster.
Shrestha is calling on the federal government to resolve the issue as soon as possible. Until then, he says his hands are tied.
"We understand the emotional pain for families who have already performed funeral rituals, but officials must work within legal boundaries to avoid future liabilities."
The government has told the BBC it is trying to find a solution.

In a statement, the prime minister's office said it was "aware of the difficulties" the law may cause families in "exceptional circumstances, including disasters". The home ministry said the government was taking the issue seriously and was ready to amend the law, if required.
The legal hurdles families are facing comes as Nepal faces a steep reconstruction bill, which the government says could cost up to £3.6bn ($4.8bn).

blocks.caption: Image caption, Relatives carry Kush grass effigies for cremation during symbolic funerals held for flood victims still reported missing

blocks.text: Image source, Getty Images
Relatives carry Kush grass effigies for cremation during symbolic funerals held for flood victims still reported missing

At the UN General Assembly in New York, Prime Minister Balen Shah explained rebuilding the country would require more than 10% of its gross domestic product, an enormous burden on the country's economy.
Dozens of public buildings including schools, health clinics and hospitals have been wrecked by the floods. That's in addition to roads, bridges, wastewater treatment plants and hydropower projects.

Shah is now pushing for grant-based international support rather than new loans. Nepal is one of the lowest emitters of global greenhouse gas emissions, yet one one of the most vulnerable countries to global warming.
"When a climate-driven disaster destroys infrastructure of a poor country, the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan or a patchwork of small grants," he told a room full of world leaders.
This is not the first time Nepal has had to recover after a devastating natural disaster.
For Tisum Ghale, the past month has been painfully familiar.
He and his family lost their home in an earthquake in 2015, and became displaced for months. They eventually settled in Betrawati.

But the place that was once a refuge is where 19 of his relatives were killed in last month's flood, including five of his sisters. He survived because he was doing construction work outside of the village.
Once again, he is without a home.
"I have lost everything," he said.

So far he has received no compensation. He desperately needs the money after his home was washed away and he looks after eight children left behind by his sisters. He is one of the thousands displaced, living across 37 holding centres in northern Nepal.
Like Lawati and thousands of other families, Ghale plans on holding a funeral without his loved ones' bodies.
He hopes the law will eventually recognise what he already knows: his loved ones will not be coming home.
Additional reporting: Rajneesh Bhandari

articles.title: US man arrested as second suspect in Canada mass school shooting planned with ChatGPT
articles.summary:
Justice department detained James Codey Bryant and allege he offered ‘technical advice’ to primary suspect

A surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school…

blocks.text: A surprise suspected accomplice has been arrested in connection with a mass school shooting in Canada that was made notorious after an 18-year-old allegedly killed six children after discussing it with the AI chatbot ChatGPT.
The US Department of Justice said Tuesday it had detained James Codey Bryant, 30, a resident of western Washington state, on a charge of conspiracy to murder persons in a foreign country.
Bryant offered money and “technical advice” to the suspected shooter for six months leading up to the killings, the justice department alleged.

Canadian police have identified the suspect in this year’s massacre of eight people – including her mother and half-brother, as well as the six children, making it the second-deadliest school shooting in the country’s history – as Jesse Van Rootselaar, who has a history of mental health problems.

It had been known that Van Rootselaar had used ChatGPT to plan the attack, which took place in February. The safety team at OpenAI, the company that owns the chatbot, flagged Van Rootselaar internally after she conducted conversations with it about gun violence, but the company did not alert police. It did reportedly close Van Rootselaar’s account, but she started a second one that was not closed. Victims’ families and the province of British Columbia have sued OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, for failing to report her behaviour.
It was not previously known publicly that Van Rootselaar was also talking to a human about her plans.

In a joint press conference with the justice department and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) on Tuesday, authorities alleged that Bryant and Van Rootselaar met on the now-defunct messaging service Omegle about three years prior to the shooting and kept in contact.

Neil Floyd, acting US attorney, and W Mike Herrington, the special agent in charge for the FBI’s Seattle bureau, said they believe Bryant sent Van Rootselaar about $100 to buy new shoes and aabout $15 for a lighter.
Authorities said there is no indication so far that the two suspects ever met in person.
According to an indictment obtained by CBC, Bryant was “knowingly and wilfully” conspiring with Van Rootselaar beginning in or before August 2025.

That August, Bryant told Van Rootselaar the pair should “find a way to delete” their messages, and in mid-December Bryant suggested getting a VPN to avoid detection for “posting a shooting video online”, according to the court document reviewed by CBC.
Police said that on several occasions Bryant tried to talk Van Rootselaar out of committing the attack, but did not contact law enforcement.

They added that after Van Rootselaar shot and killed her mother and brother in their family home, she was unable to start the car. Bryant advised her on how to turn on the engine, thereby allowing the shooter to reach the school and execute the attack, authorities said.
Bryant also allegedly agreed to livestream the mass shooting, which Harrington said police were not sure Van Rootselaar would have committed had Bryant not done so.

It was not clear whether the suspect was represented by a lawyer. Bryant will be prosecuted in the US as a US citizen under an investigation by the FBI, which said it will continue working closely with Canadian authorities.

articles.title: Fruit of the Loom, Hanes investigated over potential toxic chemicals in children's underwear
articles.summary: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton launched an investigation on Tuesday into whether Fruit of the Loom and Hanes use toxic chemicals in producing ‌children's underwear.

image.caption: Packages of Hanes underwear. The Texas attorney general launched an investigation on Tuesday into whether Fruit of the Loom and Hanes use toxic chemicals in producing ‌children's underwear. (Chuck Burton/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Health·New
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton launched an investigation on Tuesday into whether Fruit of the Loom and Hanes use toxic chemicals in producing ‌children's underwear.
Canadian company Gildan Activewear owns Hanes, says it will co-operate with investigation
· Thomson Reuters
· Posted: Oct 06, 2026 5:58 PM EDT | Last Updated: 2 minutes ago

Paxton said he sent civil investigative demands to Fruit of the Loom, which is owned by Berkshire Hathaway, and Hanes, which is owned by Canadian company Gildan Activewear, citing the chemicals' ​potential effects on children's health.
He did ​not accuse either company of wrongdoing.
Fruit of the Loom and Berkshire did not immediately respond to requests from Reuters for comment.
Montreal-based Gildan ​said it will co-operate with the investigation, and maintains ⁠strict manufacturing and ⁠sourcing standards to comply with ‌industry guidelines related to harmful chemicals.
"We remain committed to providing safe, high-quality products for consumers," it said in a statement to Reuters.
Gildan merged with Massachusetts-based HanesBrands Inc. last year in a $2.2-billion US deal.
Paxton said clothing manufacturers have turned increasingly to synthetic materials such as polyester, rayon and ⁠spandex to meet consumer demand for lower-priced products.

He said research shows that synthetic fabrics can shed microplastics, while chemicals including bisphenols, fluorine, parabens, phthalates and ‌so-called "forever chemicals" used in textile manufacturing have been associated with cancer, hormone disruption, infertility and other health concerns.
"Forever chemicals" are also known as PFAS, ​short for per- ⁠and polyfluoroalkyl substances.

items: Texas attorney general launches investigation into Lululemon's potential use of certain chemicals
New bans target PFAS in clothing. Here's how to avoid exposure (2025)

blocks.text: "We must protect our children who cannot yet protect themselves," Paxton said in a ​news release.
"This includes making sure that the necessities parents rely on are free from toxic chemicals ⁠and do not harm the health of kids."
The attorney general ⁠announced a similar probe in April into whether Vancouver-based Lululemon Athletica activewear ⁠contained "forever ⁠chemicals," which do not ​break down easily in nature.
Paxton, a Republican, is running for a U.S. Senate seat against Democrat James Talarico and trailing in most polls.
The race is among the country's most closely watched in the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

articles.title: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
articles.summary: Christa Pike, a Tennessee inmate who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday.

image.caption: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike is seen in a file photo taken Dec. 4, 2007. Pike, a Tennessee inmate who recently survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday. (J. Miles Cary/Knoxville News Sentinel/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·Updated
Christa Pike, a Tennessee inmate who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her, is awake and speaking as she receives treatment at a hospital, her attorneys said Tuesday.
Survived 2 doses of pentobarbital
Pike's attorneys said her prognosis is still "unclear" and said she faces "a long recovery."

"Against all odds, Christa Pike is conscious, speaking, and continues to receive critical medical care," attorneys for Pike said in a statement. "Despite the severe damage she endured to her arms, she is still handcuffed and shackled to the bed. Her recovery is medically unprecedented."
Her lawyers said they are grateful for the first responders and the medical team at the hospital "who treated Christa like a human and have provided exceptional care to her."
The statement was the first indication that Pike has improved since an ambulance carried her away from a Nashville prison last Wednesday.
Pike's arms left burned, blistered

Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as they attempted to put her to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The lethal injection drug didn't kill her, but her lawyers said her arms were left burned and blistered.
As recently as Sunday, her attorneys said Pike had remained unconscious and on a ventilator since the failed execution attempt.

Dr. Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery in Atlanta who consulted as an expert for Pike's legal team, said the development "bodes well for a good recovery." But he added that it could be weeks or months before anyone knows exactly what her recovery might look like or whether her competency could be restored to a level that might enable the state to try to execute her again.

"She's still in the ICU," he said. "She has recovered to a certain degree that she's able to be off a ventilator and able to speak, but in no way would I announce her free of further serious risk. There's still a lot of bad things that can happen here, even when everyone is doing their job well."

items: Tennessee prisons chief to resign after failed execution of Christa Pike, governor says
Christa Pike on ventilator after surviving Tennessee execution attempt, lawyer says

blocks.text: A spokesperson for the Tennessee Department of Correction said she could provide no information other than that Pike remained hospitalized Tuesday.
Pike's attorneys are set to go to court Wednesday as they seek to learn more about what happened in the failed lethal injection.

The attorneys are seeking a court order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence, including drug lot numbers, records and other information from the Sept. 30 attempted execution. Chancery Court Judge I'Ashea Myles scheduled a Wednesday morning status conference in the case.
Pike's attorneys said in their Tuesday statement that they continue to ask Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to commute Pike's sentence to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
"Christa is a survivor and will take recovery one day at a time," her attorneys said.

articles.title: Watch: Riot police clash with school protesters and use tear gas in France
articles.summary: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France amid a wave of protests by high-school pupils.

blocks.text: Hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets across France, as a wave of protests by high-school pupils spread to their parents, university students and unions.
Crowds of teenagers marched from the Place de la République in Paris, calling for more resources for schools, and what they called less repression from police.
Police clashed with demonstrators in Lyon, used tear gas in Paris and Marseille and water cannon in Rennes, but there was little of the serious trouble that marred previous protests.
The BBC's Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Lille.

articles.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike conscious after failed execution, lawyers say
articles.summary: Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to a statement from her lawyers on Tuesday.

blocks.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike is "conscious and speaking" after her failed execution attempt, her lawyers say.
Pike, 50, continues to receive critical medical care while handcuffed in hospital, according to a statement from her attorneys on Tuesday.

She was sentenced to death following her conviction for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995. But Pike survived two lethal injections last week and was transferred to a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, for treatment.
Her lawyers had said in the days afterwards that she was unconscious while medical staff cleared her body of the pentobarbitol injected during the failed execution attempt.
Pike's lawyers said on Tuesday that her recovery is "medically unprecedented", and while her prognosis remains unclear, "at a minimum, we expect a long recovery".
They said she is the only person known to have survived a completed execution attempt in the US.
Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee suspended all executions for the rest of the year - and the head of prisons in the state said over the weekend that he plans to resign.
Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens.
